thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts observed from 12:02:00 UTC. Error rate spiking to ~6.8% across hosted-api proxied through gateway-cluster-a. Root cause suspected: batcher queue growth / HOL blocking. Paging the oncall rota now. Paging: sarah (oncall). :rotating_light:

Sarah (oncall): I see the page — looking at dashboards. p95 token latency is normal-ish but p99 token latency and gateway 504s are up. Bulk of errors from /v1/generate path hitting batcher nodes in zone us-east-1a.

Mike (sre): Confirming. Batcher queue length on scheduler svc node set shows steady growth over last 6m. Backpressure not kicking in early enough. Sample metrics:
```
scheduler.queue.length{pool=batcher-main,zone=us-east-1a} = 1234
scheduler.enqueue.rate = 1800 req/min
batcher.processing.rate = 600 req/min
kv-cache-hits = 21%
```
Looks like head-of-line blocking: large-context requests are preventing regular short requests from being batched.

Anya (runtime): We're seeing very long KV cache fetches on a subset of GPUs (nvlink congested). Some large prefix requests (context > 12k tokens) are inflating batch sizes and holding KV slots. Possible quick mitigations: 1) apply per-request size-based preemption, 2) enable aggressive eviction policy on the batcher, 3) route large-context requests to spare small-capacity pool.

Leo (platform): I can spin up a temporary spare batcher pool (2x small gpus) and edit routing to send plan-B model-quantized variants there. But that will take ~4-6 minutes to become healthy. We should also consider increasing gateway timeouts to avoid client-side 502s while we stabilize.

Sarah (oncall): Triage decision: short-term mitigation -> enable "evict-large-prefix" policy + widen routing to fallback pool. Long-term -> throttle or reject >8k-token requests at gateway. I'll implement eviction now and coord with leo to bring up the spare pool.

Deploy-bot: runbook step executed: "set-batcher-eviction: aggressive" by sarah (oncall) at 12:05:14 UTC.

Mike (sre): After eviction flip: immediate drop in queue tail and 5xx rate down to ~3.2% within 90s. But we still see p99 latency at 1.2s higher than baseline in us-east-1a.

Alice (support): Running the customer impact checklist. A subset of paid customers (12 orgs) report intermittent 502s towards embeddings and generate. Support ticket count jumped from 2->29 in 10m. Notifying CS leads and drafting status line.

Natalie (prod-eng): Quick check — are there any recent deploys to scheduler or gateway? I see a canary deploy to scheduler yesterday but nothing at 12:00. No rolling changes in the last 30m.

Sarah (oncall): Leo — please load the spare pool and switch routing for requests with content-length > 5k tokens to it. Also bump gateway timeouts from 30s -> 45s for /v1/generate for now.

Leo (platform): spinning up spare pool: launching 4 nodes (g4-small-quant). ETA 5m. Pushing routing change to route-large-prefix policy.

Mike (sre): Command I ran to observe inflight by prefix size:
```
# metric query (promql style)
sum by (prefix_bucket) (scheduler.inflight_requests{pool="batcher-main"})
```
Prefix bucket 8k-16k has ~400 inflight requests — those are the HOL offenders.

Anya (runtime): Also toggled per-request preemption to allow small requests to preempt large ones. This is a soft preempt only (time-slice) to avoid model state corruption. Monitoring impact.

Incident-bot: Update: routing-change applied by leo at 12:10:51 UTC. Spare pool health: 3/4 nodes ready.

Sarah (oncall): Good. Monitor 5xx and p99. If 5xx < 1% for 10m, we'll start de-escalation and open a postmortem.

Mike (sre): 12:12:30 UTC — 5xx at 0.9%, gateway 504s down to baseline. Queue length trending down to normal. p99 still +400ms above baseline in the orig pool but overall customer impact reduced.

Alice (support): Notifying affected customers with an interim status: "We've applied routing and eviction mitigations; some requests may have been retried. We're monitoring and will follow up with root cause and timeline shortly." Putting this in support autopage. :email:

Natalie (prod-eng): Action item: add a router rule to cap max batch size by prefix and enforce early reject for >12k token requests with clear error payload so callers can chunk. Logged as ENG-5392.

Sarah (oncall): Handoff plan: I need to go grab quick food. handing to mike (sre) for next 2 hours. mike — keep an eye on regional drift, and coordinate with runtime if p99 doesn't settle.

Mike (sre): Acknowledged. I'll keep watch. Current mitigation summary:
- enabled aggressive eviction on batcher
- enabled per-request soft preemption
- routed large-context requests to spare pool
- bumped gateway timeout for /v1/generate to 45s temporary
- spare pool launched (4 nodes), 3 healthy

Deploy-bot: Reminder: Please revert gateway timeout to 30s and remove preemption once system stable for 20m.

Sarah (oncall): Current customer impact: 12 orgs intermittently affected, error rate peaked ~6.8%, now down to ~0.9%. No data loss. Estimated mitigation complete at 12:13:30 UTC. Post-incident follow-ups: ENG-5392 (reject large requests), ENG-5393 (improve batcher backpressure), ENG-5394 (observability: per-prefix KV fetch latency).

Mike (sre): Leaving monitoring on. If anything flares up, re-ping this thread. I'll file the incident stub and assign to natalie for RCA.

Natalie (prod-eng): Assigned RCA. I'll include telemetry from kv-cache, nvlink stats, and routing decisions. Preliminary hypothesis: combination of large-context requests causing prolonged KV fetches + insufficient backpressure thresholds.

Alice (support): Closing customer-facing note: "Issue mitigated; engineering continues root cause analysis and will provide next update in 4 hours."

Sarah (oncall): Thanks everyone. Handing off fully to mike. Going offline. :wave:
